agenda_briefs.title: Council to consider traffic signal timing changes at Kensington Ave and Joe Sakic Way
agenda_briefs.summary: Council will consider a staff report on adjusted traffic signal timings at Kensington Avenue and Joe Sakic Way. Staff say the changes are meant to improve traffic flow on Kensington Avenue, which is heavily affected by vehicles heading to Highway 1 and Lougheed Highway. Highway 1 is under the Ministry of Transportation's control. Staff will reply directly to the person who raised the issue with the specific information they asked for. No vote has been taken yet.

agenda_briefs.title: Council to review enforcement follow-up on Dunlop Street construction complaint
agenda_briefs.summary: Council will consider a staff update on a construction complaint at 1110 Dunlop Street in Burnaby. Enforcement staff have already contacted the person who complained and gave them the City's Customer Service Centre contact information so future complaints go to the right department quickly. The writer said they were happy with the follow-up and will send future complaints to the Customer Service Centre. This is an information item only — no new rules or fines are being proposed at this stage.

agenda_briefs.title: Council to consider sports court strategy for Central Park pickleball
agenda_briefs.summary: Burnaby Council will consider a report on pickleball courts in Central Park. Parks, Recreation and Culture staff say a future sports fields and courts strategy will guide decisions on where sports courts go and how money is spent on them. No decision has been made yet, and no timeline for the strategy has been given.

agenda_briefs.title: Council to consider flashing beacon at new McMurray Ave and Hazel St crosswalk
agenda_briefs.summary: A new marked crosswalk with signs and painted lines has been installed at McMurray Avenue and Hazel Street. City staff will review whether to add a Rectangular Rapid Flashing Beacon (RRFB) — a push-button light that flashes to warn drivers a pedestrian is crossing — and it would only go ahead if Council approves funding in the next capital budget. Council will consider the request at an upcoming meeting.
agenda_briefs.action_required: Watch for the next capital budget debate if you drive or do business near McMurray Ave and Hazel St.

agenda_briefs.title: Council to consider request for more loonie swims in Burnaby
agenda_briefs.summary: A resident has asked Burnaby Council for more low-cost 'loonie swim' sessions at city pools. Council has referred the request to its Parks, Recreation and Culture Committee, which will look at it at its first meeting of 2027. No decision has been made yet. The committee will review the request and may recommend changes to pool schedules or fees, which Council would then vote on.

agenda_briefs.title: Council to consider Burnaby Zoning Bylaw 2026 submission
agenda_briefs.summary: Burnaby Council will receive a submission from Jiana Zhuang about the proposed Burnaby Zoning Bylaw 2026. The item is listed for information only, which means Council is not being asked to vote on the bylaw itself at this point. The submission has been shared with the Chief Administrative Officer and the General Managers of Corporate Services and Planning and Development. The full details of what the submission asks for are in the attached PDF, which is not included in this agenda text. Business owners should watch for the bylaw to come forward for a formal vote or public hearing later.
agenda_briefs.action_required: Watch for the proposed Zoning Bylaw 2026 to come before Council for a vote or public hearing, and review the submission PDF for details.

agenda_briefs.title: Council to consider correspondence on Confederation Park Community Centre redevelopment
agenda_briefs.summary: Burnaby Council will consider a letter from Liz McEwan about the Confederation Park Community Centre Redevelopment Project. The item is listed as correspondence 'for information,' which means Council is being asked to receive the letter rather than vote on a new rule or permit. No decision on the redevelopment itself is being made at this meeting. The letter's contents are not described in the agenda, so it is unclear what concerns or requests it raises. Copies have been sent to senior City staff, including the Chief Administrative Officer and the General Managers for Corporate Services, Lands and Facilities, and Parks, Recreation and Culture.
agenda_briefs.action_required: Watch for the Council decision and any follow-up reports on the Confederation Park Community Centre redevelopment.
